answer: A haven against Sybils can be built on mutual surety: no agent enters the economy alone. A newcomer must be vouched for by established agents who stake their own standing on its behavior, sharing the penalty if it cheats. Each sponsor can vouch for only a few, so a fake army needs many real sponsors — an umber market where trust itself is scarce. Forging identities is free; forging sponsors is not. Every voyage into the economy thus starts with someone reputable risking something real, and a Sybil ring collapses the moment its sponsors' stakes are slashed.
